title: Can an app teach you a language?
text:
Millions of people use apps to learn languages. They are cheap or free, you can use them on the bus or in a queue, and they make learning feel like a game. But can you really learn a language this way?

Tom, 41, from Manchester, started learning Polish with an app two years ago because his wife is from Poznań. "The app was great at the beginning," he says. "I learned a lot of words and simple sentences. I practised for ten minutes every day, and the app sent me reminders, so I didn't forget."

But after a year, Tom had a problem. "I could read and write simple things, but when my wife's family spoke to me, I couldn't understand them. They spoke too fast!"

Language teachers say that apps are good for vocabulary and grammar, but they are not enough. To speak well, you need to talk to real people. Tom now has an online lesson with a teacher once a week, and he watches Polish films with subtitles.

"Now I can have a conversation with my mother-in-law," Tom says. "It isn't perfect, but she's very patient with me!"
